title: MrBeast × X: Creator Video Deal
summary: Deal discussion on making X a first-class home for MrBeast content. Agreed on a 12-month arrangement: full videos on X day-and-date with a guaranteed CPM floor and transparent analytics, one X-exclusive live game show with product integration for Beast brands, and a moonshot concept — a live audience-participation special around the November Mars landings. Jimmy pushed hard on ad-tech gaps; Elon committed to mid-roll ads and a brand-safety dashboard before the first upload.
decisions: 12-month deal: MrBeast main-channel videos post on X day-and-date with YouTube, with a guaranteed CPM floor for the first six months
X ships mid-roll ads and a creator brand-safety dashboard before the first full-length upload
One X-exclusive live game show in Q4 with Feastables and Lunchly integration
Develop the Mars landing live special as a joint concept, gated on SpaceX comms bandwidth
Beast Industries gets raw analytics API access, not dashboard-only metrics

action_items.task: Deliver mid-roll ad support and the brand-safety dashboard spec to the Beast team
Send the CPM floor number, the analytics API requirements, and the game show one-pager
Check with SpaceX whether Mars landing telemetry and imagery can support a live special format

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Jimmy, welcome back. Last time we tried this it was one video as an experiment. This time I want the real thing — X as an actual home for your content, not a place you cross-post clips.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: And I want that to make sense, which it currently doesn't, so let's fix it together. Real talk first? That experiment video did 200 million views on X, which sounds amazing, and it monetized at about one-eighth of what the same video earns per view on YouTube. I'm not a charity — well, I am literally also a charity, but Beast Industries isn't. I employ four hundred people. The math has to work.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Totally fair, and the math not working was our fault, not yours. Two things have changed. First, the ad system: we now have category-level brand controls, so premium advertisers can target creator content specifically. Premium video CPMs on X are up about 3x year over year. Second, I'm prepared to guarantee the math while we close the rest of the gap. Tell me the CPM floor you need and we'll write it into the deal for the first six months.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: A guaranteed floor changes the conversation completely, that's real. I'll send you the number — it'll be based on our actual YouTube RPM across the last twelve months, my team has it to the decimal. But the floor is a bridge, not a business. For this to work long-term I need three product things, and I know exactly what they are because I've spent fifteen years living inside video platforms.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: This is why I wanted you specifically. Go.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: One: mid-roll ads. My videos are twenty to forty minutes. One pre-roll on a thirty-minute video is leaving 80 percent of the revenue on the table — mid-rolls are the whole economics of long-form. Two: a real brand-safety story. My advertisers are Fortune 500. If their ad runs on my video and the reply section is a dumpster fire, I get the angry phone call, not you. I need a dashboard that shows brand-adjacency the way advertisers actually audit it. Three: raw analytics API. Not your dashboard — raw data. Retention curves second by second, traffic sources, rewatch spikes. My entire process is built on retention data. I've rewatched the first thirty seconds of my own videos more times than any human alive. No data, no deal.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: All three are doable and honestly all three make the platform better for every creator, which is the point. Mid-rolls: engineering has it half-built, I'll commit to shipped before your first upload — September 1 for the spec in your team's hands. Brand-safety dashboard: same date. Analytics API: yes, raw access, and I'd actually like your team to help spec it since you're the most sophisticated consumer of retention data on Earth.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: My analytics people will be thrilled and slightly insufferable about it. Okay, so structure. Here's what I'm comfortable with for year one: full main-channel videos on X day-and-date with YouTube. Not exclusive — I'm not moving off YouTube, let's not even have that conversation, my audience lives there. But same-day, full video, native upload, which nobody else at my scale is doing on X. That's already a big bet on you.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Day-and-date native at your scale is exactly the signal the creator ecosystem needs — if it works for the biggest, it works. I'll take that over exclusivity. But I want one thing that IS exclusive, because I need a tentpole: one live event, only on X. You're the best live-format inventor alive. Give me a game show.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: Okay, so, funny thing — I have a format I've been sitting on because it only works live and interactive, and YouTube live isn't built for it. A game show where the audience is a player. Viewers vote in real time and the votes change the game — open doors, add money to the pot, eliminate contestants. It needs sub-second voting at millions of concurrent, which is basically a poll system with the intensity of a DDoS attack. Can X handle that?

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: We handle spikes bigger than that on election nights — the vote-ingest is genuinely the easy part for us, the hard part is making the latency feel fair across continents. That's a fun problem, my kind of problem. Q4 timing? And I'm assuming Feastables and Lunchly are integrated into the show, which I'm fine with — your products in your show is the most organic ad unit that exists.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: Q4 works, probably November, and yes — the prize pyramid is literally built out of Feastables, we've done the set mockups already, it's beautiful and deeply stupid in the best way. Budget-wise, I put real money into these — the live special will cost me eight figures to produce, so the rev share on the event needs to reflect that I'm the studio here, not just the talent.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Structure it like the Taylor pilot then — for event content where the creator carries production cost, X takes the minority share. Say 80/20 your way on the event, standard split on regular uploads plus the floor. Fair?

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: Wait, hold on. Taylor Swift is doing a thing on X? You just leaked that to me, you know that, right?

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: I neither confirm nor deny, and also please don't tweet it, because I have been extremely specifically warned about announcement discipline, under threat of songwriting.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: That is the most credible threat in entertainment, I'd behave too. Okay, 80/20 on events works. Last thing on my list — actually no, the last thing is your thing. You said on the phone you had, quote, 'the biggest video idea in history' and then hung up, which was very you.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Right. So. In late November, five Starships attempt to land on Mars carrying Optimus robots. There will be live telemetry and, if the relay constellation works, near-live imagery with about a twenty-minute delay. I want the landing broadcast to be an event the whole planet watches together — and there's no one better at making twenty tense minutes into unbearable, brilliant television than you. Co-host the landing stream. Audience predictions, live models of the entry, the whole world holding its breath together on X.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: Okay, I got actual chills, and I make videos for a living so I know exactly how manufactured chills work and these are real. Yes, obviously yes, with one giant caution: we cannot game-show-ify a landing that might fail. If a ship crashes and there's a subscriber counter in the corner, we both look like clowns forever. The format has to be documentary-with-participation — reverent when it needs to be, fun when it's safe to be. I have opinions about exactly where that line is.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: That instinct is exactly why it's you and not a game show host. And there's a real technical gate: whether the comms bandwidth in those first hours supports a live format at all. I'll get the honest answer from the SpaceX team by the 26th before we design anything. If the bandwidth isn't there, we do a next-day special with the real footage instead, which is still enormous.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: Either version works for me — honestly the next-day version might be the better film. Okay, so my recap: day-and-date full uploads for twelve months with a CPM floor for six, I send you the floor number and the analytics API requirements and the game show one-pager by the 19th, you ship mid-rolls and brand-safety by September 1, live game show in November at 80/20, and we hold a slot for the Mars thing pending your bandwidth answer. And I keep the Taylor secret, which is costing me physically.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Perfect recap, you should run meetings professionally. Deal on all of it. And Jimmy — if a robot walks off that ship and a hundred million people watch it live on a stream you're hosting, that might genuinely be the most-watched moment in human history. No pressure.

transcript.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast)
transcript.text: No pressure? That's the thumbnail, Elon. That's the most clickable sentence ever spoken in a meeting. Let's go make history and also please, please don't let the robot fall over on camera.
